_why: This tool closes the operator's terminals, so every mutation here restores a way it could close the WRONG one -- most of all the caller's own pane, which is the failure the candidate row records and which no title check can prevent. The rest defend the settle-before-close order (closing an unsettled dispatch wedges its terminal permanently) and the refusals that stop it acting on a baseline it should not trust. Every mutation is born pinned to the one test it is aimed at.

mutations.name: caller-pane-is-not-excluded
mutations._mechanism: THE recorded failure: closing the operator's own agent session. Panes are indistinguishable by title, so nothing else stands in the way.

mutations.name: trust-the-baselines-self-instead-of-the-live-one
mutations._mechanism: The janitor may run from a different pane than took the snapshot; only the pane it is running in NOW is safe from itself.

mutations.name: drop-the-worktree-scope
mutations._mechanism: A concurrent agent session in a sibling worktree was live while this was written; scoping is what keeps it out.
mutations.find: if pane.get("worktreePath") == worktree and pane["handle"] not in known

mutations.name: close-without-an-explicit-handle
mutations._mechanism: `orca terminal close` takes --terminal OPTIONALLY and a bare close kills the CALLER's pane. Verified live.

mutations.name: dry-run-closes-anyway
mutations._mechanism: A dry run that mutates is worse than no dry run: it is the one mode an operator trusts.
mutations.find:
if apply:
        # `--terminal` is optional to the CLI and an omitted handle closes the
mutations.replace:
if True:
        # `--terminal` is optional to the CLI and an omitted handle closes the

mutations.name: close-before-settling
mutations._mechanism: Closing an unsettled dispatch wedges its terminal permanently -- worker-abandon and worker-stop both answer dispatch_not_found.
mutations.find: if row and str(row.get("dispatchStatus", "")).lower() not in SETTLED:

mutations.name: close-anyway-when-the-settle-failed
mutations._mechanism: Leaves a permanently wedged terminal that is also invisible. A wedged terminal you can still see beats one you cannot.
mutations.find:
outcome["skipped"] = f"settle failed ({exc.reason}); pane left open"
                return outcome
mutations.replace: outcome["skipped"] = f"settle failed ({exc.reason}); pane left open"

mutations.name: re-settle-an-already-settled-dispatch
mutations._mechanism: Mutating a completed dispatch is an unnecessary write against a Run the probe already finished with.

mutations.name: proceed-without-identifying-self
mutations._mechanism: Without a self handle there is nothing stopping the janitor from closing the session running it, so it must refuse rather than continue.

mutations.name: act-on-an-oversized-candidate-set
mutations._mechanism: A baseline taken against the wrong worktree turns every pane into a candidate; the cap is what stops that becoming a mass close.

mutations.name: accept-a-baseline-with-no-handles-key
mutations._mechanism: A malformed baseline has no keep-list at all, so every pane reads as new.
mutations.find: if not isinstance(baseline.get("handles"), list) or not baseline.get("worktree"):

mutations.name: a-failed-orca-call-reads-as-success
mutations._mechanism: 'I could not ask' must never resolve to 'there is nothing there'.

mutations.name: a-dry-run-reports-its-plan-as-done
mutations._mechanism: `PLANNED ... closed=1` reads as a pane that was closed. Same shape as a cannot-judge carrying a count: the verdict word says one thing, the fields say another, and the fields are what gets skimmed. Found by reading the tool's own live output.

mutations.name: close-unidentified-panes-by-default
mutations._mechanism: The review's headline finding: subtraction alone cannot tell the probe's panes from the operator's, so an operator pane opened after the snapshot is closed. Neither --max nor the self-handle sees it.

mutations.name: treat-every-candidate-as-identified
mutations._mechanism: Positive identification collapses back to subtraction while the counts still look reassuring.
mutations.find: (identified if pane["handle"] in workers else unidentified).append(pane)

mutations.name: leave-unidentified-panes-unnamed
mutations._mechanism: Silence is what made --max 10 insufficient: it bounded the damage at nine panes without ever saying which. A pane left alone and not reported is a pane nobody knows to look at.

mutations.name: refuse-to-close-even-with-the-explicit-flag
mutations._mechanism: The accept direction. A pane made by `terminal create` has no worker row, and that path was live-verified, so the escape hatch must actually work.
